entries.title: Pablo Jarillo-Herrero wins Kavli Prize in Nanoscience
entries.description: The MIT physicist shares the honor with two others for foundational research establishing the field of twistronics.

entries.title: How to create distinguishable states for quantum systems
entries.description: Researchers establish key insights for reading and writing information for quantum sensing, communication, computing, and control.

entries.title: Could AI tell you where you left your keys?
entries.description: A new spatial memory system for robots efficiently captures details about the objects they see while exploring their environment.

entries.title: Susan Solomon named 2026 Tang Prize laureate
entries.description: The MIT professor’s groundbreaking work on atmospheric chemistry helped lay steps towards recovery of the ozone layer and demonstrated the lasting impacts of carbon emissions on Earth’s climate.

entries.title: MIT in the media: For the future of tech, "Massachusetts can absolutely lead"
entries.description: Leaders, faculty across MIT discuss fostering innovation and talent in Greater Boston in special series of articles published alongside the outlet's annual list of 'Tech Power Players'

entries.title: A better way to model the behavior of metal alloys
entries.description: MIT researchers’ approach captures subtle atomic patterns, improving predictions of material properties.

entries.title: New chip could help tiny robots traverse complex environments
entries.description: Researchers combined an efficient algorithm with dedicated hardware to rapidly generate 3D maps for navigation using minimal memory and power.

entries.title: Computer model could enable bridges and buildings that use less material
entries.description: MIT researchers developed an approach for generating more buildable structures, bridging the gap between optimized design and real-world construction.

entries.title: What happens when environmental change outpaces life’s ability to adapt?
entries.description: A new model links Earth’s mass extinctions to mismatches between rates of environmental change and biological adaptation.

entries.title: How architecture influences political activity

entries.title: Improving the speed and energy-efficiency of AI agents
entries.description: A new system, known as Murakkab, optimizes the design and deployment of multistep workflows that power AI applications.

entries.title: MIT in the media: Exploring how curiosity-driven science is an essential ingredient in America’s success
entries.description: “Scientific American” showcases the history and future of America’s scientific engine, highlighting promising young scientists and icons at MIT and beyond.

entries.title: Students from across the Northeast step inside MIT.nano’s cleanroom
entries.description: A hands-on boot camp teaches integrated photonics to community and four-year college students in the region.

entries.title: How data centers can better manage energy use
entries.description: A new study suggests flexibility in the timing of electricity consumption could lower consumer costs.

entries.title: Antenna array could provide protected tactical satellite communications in low-Earth orbit
entries.description: The prototype array uses a small, lightweight, low-power, and low-cost aperture.

entries.title: David Autor named head of the Department of Economics
entries.description: A faculty member since 1999, Autor is a leading researcher in artificial intelligence and the work of the future.

entries.title: Graphene can hold multiple states of superconductivity, a new study finds
entries.description: What’s more, the superconducting states get stronger under conditions expected to kill them.

entries.title: Care in the midst of pressure
entries.description: Anantha P. Chandrakasan is “Committed to Caring” for redefining mentorship through presence and perspective.

entries.title: 3 Questions: Beyond data-driven aesthetics
entries.description: In a new Keller Gallery exhibition, Alexandros Haridis SM ’17, PhD ’22 traces centuries of ideas about aesthetic judgment and explores how design can make complex computational systems visible.

entries.title: Scientists find ozone depletion began decades before discovery of ozone hole
entries.description: Using modern tools, they also determined that carbon tetrachloride, used as a dry-cleaning and degreasing agent as early as the 1930s, was at the root of early ozone loss.

entries.title: Inaugural Music Technology Research Showcase celebrates work of new graduate program’s initial students
entries.description: Associate Professor Anna Huang delivers the keynote address, “In Search of Human-AI Resonance,” to a capacity crowd.

entries.title: Two MIT faculty members named 2026 Pew Biomedical Scholars
entries.description: Cell biologist Whitney Henry and immunologist Harikesh Wong will receive four years of flexible funding to advance early-career research on ferroptosis and immune decision-making.

entries.title: Q&A: What is agentic AI today, and what do we want it to be?
entries.description: Computer scientist Phillip Isola cuts through the hype to explain how AI agents work and what the future might hold for this rapidly advancing technology.

entries.title: MIT researchers advance toward greater bandwidth, more energy-efficient communications
entries.description: The FUTUR-IC research program integrates electronics and photonics in microchip systems.

entries.title: MIT student teams win top honors in NASA competition
entries.description: Three MIT teams took five top awards in the 2026 NASA RASC-AL Competition for designing critical elements for the moon base and future missions to Mars.

entries.title: The brain’s language network is more extensive than previously thought
entries.description: A new study reveals that parts of the brain located far from the canonical language-processing centers are also involved in language comprehension.

entries.title: MIT-Kalaniyot program expands, with new cohort of scholars
entries.description: The innovative effort bringing researchers from Israel to campus keeps growing while enhancing community connections and academic inquiry.

entries.title: A portable ultrasound system could make reliable breast imaging more accessible
entries.description: The new technology, which generates high-resolution, 3D images of breast tissue, requires no expertise to operate and could be used at home.

entries.title: How urban design leads to better wellness
entries.description: An extensive study of U.S. cities identifies walkable neighborhoods, urban greenery, and access to amenities as key contributors to residents’ health.

entries.title: Boleslaw Wyslouch steps down as director of Laboratory for Nuclear Science
entries.description: Wyslouch remains the director of the Bates Research and Engineering Center and will continue research on heavy ion collisions.

entries.title: MIT in the media: Innovating and educating for the next 250 years of America
entries.description: During a "Washington Post Live" panel discussion with ASU President Michael Crow, President Sally Kornbluth explored how universities are preparing the next generation of scientists to lead in America’s rapidly changing technological landscape.

entries.title: Building a scholarly community
entries.description: The SHASS Faculty Fellows Program, administered by the MIT Human Insight Collaborative, is fostering new research projects and creating space for supportive and interdisciplinary discussion.

entries.title: Why are some bacterial genes high in purines?
entries.description: In certain species of bacteria, the answer lies in shielding RNA transcripts from a quality-control factor called Rho. Understanding the requirements for expressible sequences is critical for expression engineering of therapeutic agents.

entries.title: Lerna Ekmekcioglu named head of MIT’s History Section
entries.description: A faculty member since 2011, Ekmekcioglu examines how communities survive, adapt, remember, and make claims on justice under difficult political conditions.

entries.title: Discovery helps explain why solid-state batteries often fail
entries.description: New research could help prevent the formation of tiny seeds of lithium metal within the electrolyte, enabling batteries that charge faster and last longer.

entries.title: Toward a future that preserves benefits of neurotechnology for all
entries.description: PhD student Rachel Sava, winner of the Envisioning the Future of Computing Prize, explores transformative improvements and dystopian risks of neural technology.

entries.title: Jesse Thaler named director of the Laboratory for Nuclear Science
entries.description: The professor of physics and inaugural director of the NSF AI Institute for Artificial Intelligence and Fundamental Interactions will lead LNS and continue his research in particle physics.

entries.title: Hydrogen: clean fuel of the future — if we can find a cheap and clean way to ship it
entries.description: A team led by MIT Energy Initiative researchers developed the HyCAT tool, enabling decision-makers to explore the cost and carbon emissions of their options for shipping hydrogen fuel to their site.

entries.title: Many black holes had past lives, new research shows
entries.description: Physicists have found signs of colliding black holes that are themselves products of previous black hole smash-ups.

entries.title: How novice coders can develop AI programs for military applications
entries.description: A USAF cadet and a Lincoln Laboratory researcher found AI chatbots can help nontechnical service members produce viable software applications for their unique problems.

entries.title: The brain’s internal ruler
entries.description: A simple brain circuit measures objects’ distance from the body using touch signals from a rodent’s whiskers, MIT scientists find.

entries.title: MIT engineers whip up a more breathable hydrogel
entries.description: The new aerated material could enable longer-lasting bandages, implants, and wearable sensors.

entries.title: MIT researcher proposes a way to detect nuclear weapons in space
entries.description: The 1967 Outer Space Treaty bans nuclear weapons in space, but there’s currently no way to verify that satellites aren’t carrying them.

entries.title: MIT-designed educational factory embraces modern manufacturing
entries.description: MIT and Tec de Monterrey will expand FrED curriculum to universities across Mexico.

entries.title: Separating logic and language
entries.description: Neuroscientists find logical reasoning does not involve language-processing parts of the brain.

entries.title: Ana Miljački named head of the Department of Architecture
entries.description: In this leadership role, Miljački seeks to shepherd a collective commitment to transform the present into a better future.

entries.title: Bringing the data to every sideline
entries.description: PhD candidate Henry Wang works with FIFA and other organizations to advance the way sports are played, analyzed, and refereed.

entries.title: Tiny robot boats build floating structures
entries.description: MIT researchers developed FloatForm, a swarm of small aquatic robots that snap together like ants forming a raft, assembling into reconfigurable structures on the water.

entries.title: A baseball-sized sensor can detect chemical threats
entries.description: The “TOSSIT” device, developed at MIT Lincoln Laboratory, can warn service members and first responders of dangerous vapors and aerosols.

entries.title: Beyond the pitch: The founder’s journey
entries.description: An MIT mechanical engineering course explores entrepreneurship through lessons and stories shared by alumni startup founders.

entries.title: New flapping robot swims and flies like a diving bird
entries.description: MIT engineers’ design could lead to a new class of aerial-aquatic vehicles for ocean exploration.

entries.title: MIT-led project opens first climate shelter in Bangladesh
entries.description: The Jameel Observatory-CREWSnet project opens a solar-powered “adaptation fortress” in Satkhira, a region facing severe and growing climate threats.

entries.title: Discovery could lead to brighter, more energy-efficient digital displays
entries.description: Researchers found a simple solution for extending the lifespans of LEDs made from glowing microscopic particles called quantum dots.

entries.title: New method aims to keep kids safe from illegal AI-generated content
entries.description: Researchers developed an auditing technique to test generative AI models for malicious capabilities, without prompting them for illegal outputs.

entries.title: Tiny infrared chip could improve detection of gases and heat
entries.description: The tunable device controls mid-infrared light for more precise thermal imaging, chemical sensing, or pollution monitoring.

entries.title: AI agents create virtual playgrounds to help robots get crucial training data
entries.description: “SceneSmith” system uses collaborative AI agents to create realistic 3D environments of places like kitchens, hotels, and living rooms, where robots can simulate everyday chores.

entries.title: How MIT students are helping to prevent cyberattacks
entries.description: Students from the MIT Cybersecurity Clinic help local governments and other vulnerable organizations defend against digital threats.

entries.title: Arthur Bahr named head of MIT’s Literature Section
entries.description: A faculty member since 2007, the scholar of medieval literature explores how different parts of physical manuscripts combine to create interest and meaning.

entries.title: MIT engineers find a precise way to grow artificial blood vessels
entries.description: Gently stretching and pulling a “blood vessel on a chip” encourages controlled sprouting of new vessels, for possible use in artificial tissues or organs.

entries.title: Can AI build a jet engine? JARVIS Challenge tests role of AI copilots in tough-tech engineering
entries.description: MIT students designed, built, and tested a jet engine with AI copilots, assessing AI’s usefulness in developing high-performance aerospace systems.

entries.title: How visual learning happens in the brain
entries.description: Scientists find that learning to identify a new object subtly reshapes visual processing in the brain.

entries.title: Three MIT Press journals lead their fields with Clarivate No. 1 rankings

entries.title: Helping AI models to meet the real world
entries.description: Through research and entrepreneurship, Professor Devavrat Shah is helping to design methods that can handle constant decision-making using limited computational resources.

entries.title: Electric fields help guide neural activity, even from moment to moment

entries.title: 3D-printed bridge points the way to greener construction
entries.description: MIT researchers developed a framework that folds a printer’s real-world limits into the optimization, while revealing that better hardware could sharply reduce material use.

entries.title: MIT Professor Susumu Tonegawa, renowned molecular biologist and Nobel laureate, dies at 86
entries.description: Tonegawa made landmark discoveries about how the immune system generates antibody diversity and how the brain forms memories.

entries.title: 3 Questions: Neural transparency and the future of AI design
entries.description: Assistant Professor Pat Pataranutaporn describes a new interface that lets everyday users glimpse inside an AI's neural network before their chatbot ever says a word.

entries.title: A better way to turn 2D designs into 3D models for rapid prototyping
entries.description: Researchers developed an automated framework that helps AI models generate CAD programs more accurately and efficiently.

entries.title: For energy systems that power a reliable grid, the future is all about location
entries.description: MIT researchers find that where new energy projects are built could be key to avoiding blackouts in a future with hotter weather and other challenges.

entries.title: Diana Grass: Listening to the body’s language
entries.description: The PhD candidate builds soft bioelectronic technologies to decode signals between the brain and the rest of the body.

entries.title: How an influx of salt may affect microbial ecosystems

entries.title: Following the questions where they lead
entries.description: Assistant Professor Bailey Flanigan has arrived at complex computational methods for helping democracy thrive.

entries.title: School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences welcomes six new faculty for 2026
entries.description: New professors join the Comparative Media Studies/Writing, Economics, Linguistics, and Music and Theater Arts departments.

entries.title: Emery Brown, Daniel Hastings, and Douglas Lauffenburger named Institute Professors
entries.description: Longtime professors and experts in the fields of anesthesiology, aerospace engineering, and biological engineering, respectively, receive MIT’s highest faculty honor.

entries.title: MIT honors employees with 2026 Excellence Awards, Collier Medal, and Staff Award for Distinction in Service

entries.title: Engineering Design Studio hosts alumni on their fifth, 10th … and 55th reunions
entries.description: A recent reunion activity, taught by EECS Senior Lecturer Gim Hom, doubled as both his “last class” and a chance to reconnect with classmates.

entries.title: Diffuse puffs of “missing” matter surround most galaxies

entries.title: Professor Emeritus Dimitri Bertsekas, influential computer scientist and prolific author, dies at 83

entries.title: MIT student leaders: Q&A with men’s soccer captain Dilin Meloni

entries.title: MIT projects selected for funding under US Department of Energy’s Genesis Mission
entries.description: Initial research projects advance national priorities across natural resources, manufacturing, nuclear physics, and more.

entries.title: Looking beyond research

entries.title: MIT engineers design recyclable elastic yarn

entries.title: Making robots faster by helping them think ahead

entries.title: Yu Deng ’11 and Hong Wang PhD ’19 awarded Fields Medal
entries.description: MIT-trained mathematicians earn the honor, one of the most prestigious in the field, for their significant achievements.

entries.description: Architect of MIT’s interdisciplinary Program in Polymers and Soft Matter and the PhD in chemical engineering practice is remembered for his passion for mentorship and education.

entries.title: How a medical database developed at MIT evolved into a global standard of data-sharing

entries.title: Why some nitrogen-processing enzymes are more efficient than others

entries.title: Connecting research to policy on Capitol Hill
entries.description: MIT students and postdocs discussed science funding and research with policymakers in Washington during the MIT Science Policy Initiative’s annual Congressional Visit Days.

entries.title: Daniela Rus receives Bavarian Minister-President's High-Tech Prize
entries.description: Director of CSAIL and MIT professor honored for her contributions to robotics, artificial intelligence, and autonomous systems.

entries.title: Building energy security through more sustainable batteries

entries.title: Using reason, again and again

entries.title: Turning molecules into reliable electronic devices

entries.title: Connecting students with the future of microelectronics
entries.description: The 2026 NEMC Hub-sponsored externship gave students access to world-class research, advanced semiconductor manufacturing, and professionals driving innovation across the Northeast.

entries.title: Alexander Rakhlin named director of  the MIT Statistics and Data Science Center
entries.description: An expert in machine learning, statistics, and computation, Rakhlin succeeds Professor Ankur Moitra.

entries.title: The benefits of medical AI assistance vary based on user expertise

entries.title: Solving the solvent problem

entries.title: Reframing leadership as a design problem

entries.title: Past is prologue for geopolitical developments

entries.title: These 3D-printed objects can tell you if they’re being used properly
entries.description: The “ShiftLens” design and fabrication system creates objects that change their surface appearance based on user interactions, without any electronics.

entries.title: Researchers make air-stable, ultrathin superconductors, for more scalable quantum devices

entries.title: Scientists unveil more than 600 new tissue models of human cancer
entries.description: Derived from patient tumor samples and available to researchers around the world, the cells will aid the development of new cancer treatments.

entries.title: Then and now: How MIT Lincoln Laboratory has served as a driving force in national security innovation
entries.description: Members of the laboratory community reflect on technology impacts that shaped the United States and the world over the past 75 years.

entries.title: A new way to watch heat move through electronics
entries.description: MIT researchers can now precisely measure how heat moves through multilayered materials like computer chips.

entries.title: Akirah Bradley-Armstrong named vice chancellor for student life
entries.description: An experienced student affairs leader is joining MIT to oversee the next chapter for the Division of Student Life.

entries.title: Physicists watch a material’s electrons assemble, and reassemble, into coexisting phases
entries.description: The study could help scientists understand how superconductivity and other more complex phenomena emerge in quantum materials.

entries.title: MIT researchers tackle the economic realities of fusion power
entries.description: Their new study aims to give budding industry a framework for understanding how fusion can be profitable.

entries.title: High-orbit satellites could light the way for travel to the moon

entries.title: With a feel for physics, AI models simulate a wider range of real-world scenarios

entries.title: On the hunt for dark matter

entries.title: The mystery of the Chinese tea chest label

entries.title: 3 Questions: MIT Sloan launches Evening MBA

entries.title: How to design a space habitat that supports its residents’ mental health

entries.title: Met Warehouse opens as the new home of MIT’s School of Architecture and Planning
entries.description: In a feat of adaptive reuse, a massive, century-old brick storage facility has been turned into a contemporary hub for collaboration and creative work.

entries.title: Astronomers discover a brand-new type of astrophysical object: A black hole star
entries.description: The mashup of a black hole and an enormous star has never been seen before and could explain the mysterious little red dots often found in deep-space images.

entries.title: MIT selected to lead new NSF materials research center
entries.description: The Materials Research Science and Engineering Center unites researchers across disciplines to develop technologies for medical imaging, sustainable metals production, and next-generation electronics.

entries.title: Featured video: An “MIT story” about an iconic professor
entries.description: A new short film from MIT Open Learning explores the influential career of Institute Professor and School of Engineering Dean Paula Hammond.

entries.title: Researchers uncover hidden pore network within nuclear fuel
entries.description: New understanding of how nuclear fuel breaks down and changes in an operating nuclear reactor could help keep some reactors running longer, will inform the next generation of nuclear reactor fuel systems.

entries.title: High-speed microscopy reveals electrical activity across the brain
entries.description: The new technique could help scientists learn how the entire brain works to generate decisions and emotions.

entries.title: Cells pulse together as they grow — and malignant cells pulse the longest
entries.description: MIT researchers discovered a cellular dance that may offer clues to the development of cancer, asthma, and other diseases.

entries.title: Drug that targets an inflammatory enzyme could help prevent lung cancer
entries.description: A new study by MIT researchers shows that inhibiting caspase-1 can reduce the risk of tumor growth.

entries.title: Professor Emeritus Chiang Chung Mei, pioneering scholar of ocean wave dynamics and fluid mechanics, dies at 91
entries.description: A towering figure in theoretical hydrodynamics is remembered for his intellectual rigor, generosity, and lifelong devotion to his students.

entries.title: Flexible brain circuits can switch between different tasks
entries.description: Neuroscientists have discovered circuits in the prefrontal cortex that can be repurposed to store different types of information.

entries.title: MIT engineers connect bacteria to create living transistors
entries.description: By wiring together colonies of these bacteria, the researchers built circuits that can perform complicated calculations.

entries.title: Mathematical framework connects biological principles to manufacturable, adaptive materials
entries.description: The new framework could streamline the design process of robotic grippers or aerospace components that exhibit complex behaviors found in nature.

entries.title: Q&A: Rethinking how innovation happens
entries.description: In his latest book, Professor Eugene Fitzgerald examines the forces that turn breakthroughs into value — and why innovation resists simple formulas.

entries.title: DNA shaper steers nervous system development
entries.description: A study of worms finds a protein that helps shape the structure of the genome is critical for establishing the identity of some neurons.

entries.title: How 35 percent of US employees are left on the margins
entries.description: In a new book, Paul Osterman details his research finding more than one-third of the country’s workers are “disposable,” with little security or chance of job advancement.

entries.title: Tackling rare genetic disorders with patient-focused science
entries.description: Shannon Knight, a brain and cognitive sciences PhD candidate and McGovern Institute researcher, focuses on developing a novel gene therapy.

entries.title: Anthea Coster awarded International Union of Radio Science Appleton Prize
entries.description: The MIT Haystack Observatory principal research scientist is honored for lifetime contributions to ionospheric research.

entries.title: When AI art has no author: Study finds generated images often can’t be traced to training data

entries.title: Cell-preservation technique could make CAR-T cell therapy more accessible
entries.description: MIT researchers’ approach, which uses naturally occurring sugars as antifreeze, could make it easier for hospitals to deploy this type of cancer treatment.

entries.title: Startup brings ancient Roman concrete technology to modern construction
entries.description: Dmat is commercializing findings from the lab of Associate Professor Admir Masic to make concrete longer-lasting and more sustainable.

entries.title: Securing wireless communication in next-generation devices

entries.title: Flipping the script on biology education, and scaling it up

entries.title: Creating innovations that scale across borders
entries.description: A new book coauthored by Professor Amos Winter asserts that, to solve major challenges and deliver products of value to consumers in both developed and emerging markets, innovators must think and act globally.

entries.title: How the Toxoplasma parasite adapts to crowded conditions in host cells
entries.description: A new study by Whitehead Institute researchers identifies how the widespread parasite Toxoplasma gondii survives in crowded environments in infected cells, which helps it persist in long-lasting brain cysts.

entries.title: The game’s the thing
entries.description: MIT senior Kayode Dada has a passion for designing games, and a penchant for building community.

entries.title: MIT engineers design a better controller for operating construction diggers
entries.description: The new, more intuitive system could speed up the training process for excavator operators.

entries.title: Paving the way for greener ammonia production
entries.description: New MIT research could lead to better materials for a fossil-fuel-free process for making the chemical that's essential to fertilizer and other products.

entries.title: The importance of indoor airflow patterns in spreading airborne disease
entries.description: Researchers explore how a key factor can mitigate or promote tuberculosis transmission.

entries.title: Language skills stay strong in older adults, even while other cognitive abilities decline
entries.description: MIT researchers find that activity in the brain’s language network is nearly identical in young and old people.

entries.title: Generating scenarios for extreme events, without extreme data
entries.description: A new algorithm learns to anticipate the unprecedented scenarios that critical infrastructure and global supply chains are least prepared for.

entries.title: Meteorite dust holds records of magnetism that may have helped form the sun
entries.description: The discovery likely represents the earliest known evidence of a magnetic field in the infant solar system.

entries.title: Brain circuit keeps tabs on what just happened to aid judgment of what’s happening now
entries.description: To keep track of what’s going on in front of it, the brain relies not only on what it sees, but also a comparison with what it just saw. A new study pinpoints the circuit that provides that service.

entries.title: The secret love life of the longfin squid
entries.description: MIT Sea Grant resident artist and acclaimed underwater photographer Keith Ellenbogen captures an intimate look at courtship and communication in a hidden spawning spectacle off Cape Cod.

entries.title: A new kind of aircraft departs an MIT classroom and arrives at an Ohio factory
entries.description: Electra’s hybrid, fixed-wing aircraft, which grew out of a class project, could make travel easier for passengers taking shorter trips.

entries.title: Cells use a little-known molecule to protect themselves from iron overload

entries.title: Retooling to help democracy revive

entries.title: AI helps design new materials that work in the real world

entries.title: MIT student leaders: Q&A with McCormick Hall co-president Sydney Baller
entries.description: The rising senior loves her dorm and its community and wants to serve as a bridge to its next residents as the building heads into renovations.

entries.title: MIT engineers create a system for building shape-changing smart devices

entries.title: New type of attack can slip past the defenses in your computer’s processor

entries.title: Looking beyond natural sequences
entries.description: A new machine-learning framework aims to improve the success rate of computational protein design while moving away from results that reproduce sequences found in nature.

entries.title: Gage Coon: An Earth scientist exploring the power of microbes
entries.description: The PhD student’s research on how microorganisms digest compounds in their environment could enable advances in wastewater treatment.

entries.title: How MIT Sandbox has turned student ideas into $8.7 billion in global impact
entries.description: Through a decade of non-dilutive funding, hands-on mentorship, and a safe space to fail fast, the MIT Sandbox Innovation Fund Program has helped students translate curiosity into real-world impact.

entries.title: How an MIT graduate student helped a team of young scientists test their experiment at CERN

entries.title: Archived: Building 18 Updates
entries.description: Photo: Emily Dahl

entries.title: How an MIT research project became a global programming language
entries.description: With millions of users across the world, Julia has been used to conduct cutting-edge research and to design new drugs, jet engines, heat pumps, and more.

entries.title: Study: Peptides can form well-defined structures in harsh, Venus-like conditions
entries.description: New research offers support for the possibility that complex biological molecules could exist in the highly acidic environment of Venus’s cloud layer.

entries.title: Playing against climate risk
entries.description: Climate scientist Sai Ravela is using games to help coastal communities find creative adaptations to climate change.

entries.title: MIT Quantum Initiative launches postdoctoral fellowship program
entries.description: The Institute welcomes its first cohort of QMIT Fellows this fall to advance interdisciplinary quantum research.

entries.title: At MIT convocation, a warm welcome for the Class of 2030
entries.description: The Institute is “so glad and so grateful” to have this year’s new undergraduates aboard, President Kornbluth said at the annual greeting ceremony.

entries.title: Gulfstream IV makes its long-awaited return to Lincoln Laboratory
entries.description: The modified aircraft will support an ongoing US Air Force program to assess and enhance the survivability of air and space vehicles.

entries.title: Translating economic growth into better lives
entries.description: Graduate student Lyonel Tanganco investigates how to improve public policy interventions and address challenges in nutrition, climate, and development.

entries.title: Ila Kumar: Innovating with communities
entries.description: The PhD student works to give young people an active role in shaping digital technologies that can support their own well-being.

entries.title: Atlas of the brain’s striatum could guide researchers to new drug treatments
entries.description: A new study reveals insights into populations of neurons affected by Huntington’s disease, schizophrenia, addiction, and other disorders.

entries.title: Cognition and consciousness arise from analog computations, says new theory
entries.description: The brain's ability to generate quick, nimble volitional thought — and a unified awareness of thought and experience — arises from analog computations, MIT neuroscientists argue in a new review.

entries.title: Walter Torous named executive director of MIT Center for Real Estate
entries.description: The senior lecturer, already director of the degree program, will now oversee all aspects of the center’s activities and operations.

entries.title: New research shows a neutrino laser is impossible
entries.description: Due to physical and fundamental limitations, an earlier proposal for producing laserlike beams of neutrinos cannot be achieved, scientists report.

entries.title: System helps humans predict when self-driving cars will make mistakes
entries.description: A new method, called CW-Net, translates the reasoning process of an autonomous vehicle’s AI system into understandable concepts that explain its behavior.

entries.title: From MIT to IBM, expediting AI and quantum deployment
entries.description: MIT affiliates engage with the MIT-IBM Computing Research Lab to bring rigorous theory to production systems.

entries.title: Building foundations that last
entries.description: Assistant Professor Iwnetim Abate creates space for ambitious research and sustainable growth for his graduate students.

entries.title: New qubit architecture enables faster, more accurate operations
entries.description: This advance could be a big step toward developing a scalable, practical quantum computer.

entries.title: Giving farmers a more sustainable way to protect crops
entries.description: Led by Andee Wallace PhD ’20, Robigo uses cutting-edge biotechnology to engineer microbes to fight pests, reducing the need for harmful chemical pesticides.

entries.title: Fabrication platform could enable flexible, transparent next-generation photonic chips
entries.description: This scalable process produces high-performance chips for applications like discreet wearables or pliable augmented-reality displays.

entries.title: Associate Professor Thomas Rose, an expert in archaeometallurgy, dies at 37
entries.description: Colleagues remember Rose as an enthusiastic and gracious friend who had recently started a promising research track at MIT.

entries.title: 3 Questions: The essential role of international engagement
entries.description: Duane Boning, MIT’s vice provost for international activities, discusses the Institute’s approach to global engagement.

entries.title: Faculty receive promotions in the School of Architecture and Planning for 2026
entries.description: The range of faculty disciplines showcases the breadth of research and scholarship across the school.

entries.title: New method allows scientists to follow gene activity over time in the same cells
entries.description: In the new method, cells package and export their RNA, enabling researchers to sequence and analyze the RNA without killing the cells.

entries.title: Stories from the steel mills: A model for sharing workers’ histories
entries.description: MIT anthropologist Chris Walley developed a project for people in Southeast Chicago to tell their histories — an approach any community can adopt.

entries.title: How architects turned a hulking brick box into MIT’s newest academic hub
entries.description: A venerable storage facility has become a 21st-century architectural tour de force. Here are the key decisions that transformed the Met Warehouse.

entries.title: Governor Healey, MIT President Kornbluth to Kick Off Festivities at MIT Future Fest
entries.description: The five-day festival will explore the future of science, technology, art and design from Wednesday, Sept. 30 to Sunday, Oct. 4

entries.title: Researchers tune into Arctic under-ice sounds and test through-ice communication
entries.description: The work is part of a multiyear effort to develop a distributed sensor network for relaying data collected from this critical region.

entries.title: Study predicts large disparities in access to food, water, and energy in 2050
entries.description: In some regions of the world, the poorest people may spend about 50 percent of their income on food, while the richest spend about 5 percent.

entries.title: An electrochemical approach turns ammonia into pure hydrogen
entries.description: An MIT team has demonstrated a more efficient way to extract pure hydrogen gas from hydrogen carrier molecules.
